In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed receiver is a viable alternative to existing detectors for coherent pulse train detection in compound Gaussian distributed clutter.

the proposed detector is the optimum detector for a large class of clutter apdfs, including the Rayleigh distribution, the K distribution, the Nakagami-m distribution, and the generalized Nakagami-m (GNm) distribution, and that it is a very good detector for the remaining clutter apdfs.
the proposed receiver, which does not require any a priori information about the clutter envelope distribution, is the most powerful CFAR detector available for this application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed detector, which is a generalization of the optimum receiver for the case of Gaussian apdf, achieves a performance which is very close to the one of the optimum receiver, but does not rely on any apdf knowledge.

the receiver is capable of achieving a performance very close to that of the optimum structure, even when the apdf is not available, while at the same time it does not require a large number of pulses to be integrated.
the proposed receiver, although not optimum, provides a good tradeoff between the computational complexity and the detection performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a large class of apdfs, the clutter envelope can be treated as a nuisance parameter, whose knowledge is not needed to achieve CFAR.
the structure of the covariance matrix is a more relevant parameter than its amplitude statistics in the design of optimum detectors in compound-Gaussian clutter.
the structure of the covariance matrix is sufficient to design detectors that are asymptotically optimum for a wide class of apdf's.
